claim: Performance and capacity-censored demand feed a financial chain whose valuation and feasibility constraints support rolling player and leverage decisions.

manuscript_evidence.supports: Elo performance model maps game information to expected wins.
Capacity-censored attendance demand and dynamic ticket pricing.
Revenue, operating/salary costs, interest, profit and cash; revenue/EBITDA/DCF valuation lenses; target-leverage borrowing/repayment.
No move/sign/trade decisions, salary/cash/debt feasibility and rolling updates using available information.
Injury, interest-rate and market-size scenarios; Monte Carlo and sensitivity analysis.

model_relationships.meaning: Attendance and pricing drive ticket revenue
Subtract operating costs, salaries and interest
Financial position supports valuation checks and constrained decisions
Player-action changes and information updates; not look-ahead forecasting

references.borrowed: Source Our Works overview at PDFp4 was visually inspected. Retain the performance-to-value chain and decision constraints; replace crowded serpentine boxes with a straight chain and outer feedback route.
references.not_borrowed: Source pixels, layout coordinates, paper-specific numerical results, team/award labels and unsupported causal claims.

caption: Conceptual overview of a sports-team decision model. Elo-based performance drives capacity-constrained attendance and revenue, which enters a financial ledger and valuation cross-checks. Player actions and financing are evaluated under cash, debt and salary constraints and updated as games are observed. Scenario and sensitivity checks remain separate from the main operating chain. No numerical forecast or investment recommendation is reproduced.
placement: End of Introduction / Our Work, before assumptions. Intended 180mm full-text width; physical print proof pending.

checks: Five-stage sequence distinguishes revenue from profit/cash.
Attendance capacity limit and censored demand remain explicit.
Revenue, EBITDA and DCF shown as valuation cross-checks, not an invented weighted formula.
No move/sign/trade, target leverage, cash floor, debt limit and salary cap are visible.
Feedback labelled Update as games are observed returns to performance; exogenous scenarios grouped separately.
Removed dark background and accidental printed section/page instructions; final title and labels readable.
No numeric business outcome or code execution result is shown.

source_notes: Direct PDF intake encountered malformed font surrogate text. The session uses the previously extracted complete 32-page text with affected glyphs replaced; the original overview was visually inspected. PDF SHA remains recorded separately.
Author repository code is a later reconstruction, not independently verified competition execution. This example uses the paper only.
Source baseline uses revenue multiples; EBITDA/DCF are comparison lenses. Injury is drawn as a scenario, not a validated stochastic process.
